issues.description: The official fix location (ZipMisc.unzip) is not patched. If the CVE's zip-slip class is reachable through that separate extraction sink, it remains exploitable; our patch only closes the Main.java splash-cache path from the taint trace.

getEntry() now returns null on refusal, a value not previously produced on this path; if any caller dereferences it without a null check, a malicious entry could trigger an NPE rather than clean handling.
Small TOCTOU window: canonical containment is checked, but actual getInputStream/extraction happens a few lines later; a symlink swapped in between is a theoretical (low-risk) bypass.

result.summary: Our patch applies the correct CWE-022 defense of record — canonicalize the resolved entry path (resolving symlinks and ../) then verify it stays inside the cache directory, with a trailing File.separator to block sibling-prefix bypass — placed precisely at the traced sink in Main.java.getEntry(). It eliminates the observed POV and passes regressions, and is technically sound. However, it fixes a different location than the official fix (ZipMisc.unzip), so if the vulnerability class is also reachable via that separate extraction sink, that path remains unguarded.
result.root_cause: Untrusted jar entry names (jarEntry) are joined to a base directory and used to open/extract a file without verifying the resolved path stays within the intended directory, allowing path traversal / zip-slip at the extraction sink.
